title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: THE LEAD — Claude Code 2.1.261 (September 4) ships /skill-doctor, a first-party tool that reports which loaded skills go UNUSED and what each one COSTS IN CONTEXT, so they can be pruned; for a fleet carrying ~130 skills this is the first time the vendor has offered a measurement of the thing this ecosystem has only ever added to
bullets.summary: Date read off the primary: <Update label="2.1.261" description="September 4, 2026">, with 2.1.260 (September 3) beneath it. Four additions matter. (a) /skill-doctor — in the vendor's own words, 'show which loaded skills go unused and what they cost in context, so you can prune them'. (b) bashOutputMaxChars and taskOutputMaxChars raise how much command and background-task output Claude receives inline before it is spilled to a file, up to 128K characters. (c) --append-subagent-system-prompt-file reads a subagent system prompt from a file, for prompts too large to pass on the command line. (d) Auto mode now treats a link that packs content into a public diagram renderer's URL as an upload to that site, no longer auto-approved unless you asked for it. Two fixes land on paths this environment uses daily: Claude in Chrome file_upload failing with 'paths: expected array, received undefined' in local Cowork sessions run from the Claude Desktop app, and SendMessage to an offline Remote Control session on another machine reading as delivered when delivery was only queued. Also fixed: resuming a session losing hook output and other context around parallel tool calls, which changed the resumed request; sustained high CPU when a background agent could not be resumed and its wake-up was retried in a tight loop; and in-process agent-team teammates re-sending their first-turn tool and skill announcements on the second turn, changing the request prefix and missing the prompt cache. A large VS Code block accompanies it, including an Add/Remove form for MCP servers inside the IDE.
bullets.how: YES — the first bullet in this corpus that hands the fleet a MEASUREMENT instead of an argument. The skill count has only ever grown, every loaded skill is context spent whether or not it fires, and until today the only way to know which ones earned their place was to guess. /skill-doctor turns that into a report. Concrete sequence: run claude --version (now a SEVENTH consecutive day as the unread prerequisite, and 2.1.260's parentheses bug — a permission rule silently dropped, leaving folders marked read-only actually writable — keeps it a security question in a tree full of parenthesised paths like _RECOVERED_2026-06-24), upgrade, then run /skill-doctor in a normal working session and keep the output as a baseline to re-run monthly. taskOutputMaxChars is directly useful to this very job, whose sub-fetches routinely exceed the inline cap and spill to files. The diagram-renderer change is a quiet exfiltration fix worth knowing about for any agent that renders content through a third-party URL. No bearing on Brand 9 or PRAGMA.

bullets.title: THE PLATFORM CHANNEL WAS NOT SILENT — this report recorded 'Anthropic Platform silent a FIFTH consecutive day' across all three fires yesterday, and today's fetch of the same page shows a '### September 3, 2026' heading carrying ant apply: resources-as-code for AGENTS, ENVIRONMENTS, SKILLS, MEMORY STORES and DEPLOYMENTS, with a claude-lock.json lockfile
bullets.summary: Version 1.30.0 of the ant CLI adds ant apply, which creates and updates those five resource types from files in your repository: describe each resource in a file, run ant apply, approve the plan it prints, and commit the claude-lock.json lockfile it writes so that later runs, on your machine or in CI, update the same resources instead of creating new ones. The entries beneath it are September 1 (Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1, cache reads $0.25/MTok, tool_choice any/tool returning 400, per-message effort beta) and August 27, with the August 19-20 entries being the ones that took computer use, browser use, Agent Skills and the Files API out of beta. Note what this does to yesterday's record: the surface WAS opened, three separate times, by the correct rule, and this entry was not visible on any of those reads.
bullets.how: YES, two ways. Substantively this is the missing half of bullet 1: one tool tells you which skills earn their context, the other lets a skill library, its agents and its memory stores be declared in files, version-controlled, and applied idempotently with a plan step and a lockfile. That is the shape this ecosystem's ~130 skills and its Hermes cron jobs already want and currently get by hand, session by session. The plan-then-approve step is the same approval gate Mallard runs under; the lockfile is the same one-canonical-file discipline the corpus already encodes; and 'update the same resources instead of creating new ones' is a direct answer to the drift this fleet fights whenever a skill or job is rebuilt from memory. Methodologically it is the sharper lesson and is written up in bullet 4. No bearing on Brand 9 or PRAGMA.

bullets.title: CORRECTION, carried at its true date — Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 has a SECOND PRICE LIST: muse-spark-1.3-contributor at $0.10/$0.20 per MTok against the standard $1.25/$4.25, with cached input falling from $0.15 to $0.002 (a 75x cut), and the consideration is that every prompt, response and usage pattern on that tier enters Meta's training pipeline
bullets.summary: Dated September 3, so outside today's window, and named here as a CORRECTION rather than as news. Yesterday's report discussed Muse Spark 1.3's cost per task rising from $0.40 to $0.55 and treated it purely as a price movement, missing that Meta had simultaneously published a tier roughly 95% cheaper on average — up to 21x on the headline comparison — priced in data rather than dollars. Muse Spark is explicitly aimed at coding and other agentic applications, which is precisely the workload whose prompts and outputs would be handed over. The discount is not a promotion with an end date; it is a standing second SKU.
bullets.how: MAYBE — not as a routing recommendation but as a governance line worth stating BEFORE someone finds the number attractive. The work this fleet's agents do is exactly the work that would be contributed: client site content, GSC/GA pulls, B9 answer-page drafts, credentialed deploy sequences, PRAGMA method. A 95% discount on an agentic-coding model is genuinely large, and this corpus has no standing rule about training-data tiers at all, which is the gap this bullet exists to name — the decision should be made deliberately once and written down, not discovered later in a bill or a client conversation. The transferable form is broader than Meta and extends yesterday's rule: per-token price is not cost, and now, cheaper is not always paid in money. For Brand 9 and PRAGMA the client-confidentiality read is the same and points the same way.

bullets.title: NULL SWEEP + METHOD — the Platform null broke for a NEW reason: not an unchecked channel (yesterday's lesson) but a CHECKED channel that gained a back-dated entry after being read. Frontier null for September 4-5, no MCP release a SEVENTH week, no arXiv paper in window, no material agent round in window, and the signage MCP negative holds an EIGHTEENTH day
bullets.summary: ANTHROPIC, all four surfaces opened per yesterday's corrected checklist: Platform release notes newest heading '### September 3, 2026' (bullet 2); Claude Code changelog newest 2.1.261 / September 4, 2026 (bullet 1); claude.com/blog newest still the two September 2 commerce-agent posts (the announcement and the anatomy deep-dive); anthropic.com/news newest still Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 dated Sep 1, 2026, with Aug 27's Model Hardware Standard preview beneath. FRONTIER: no model release dated September 4 or 5 from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere; newest remains GPT-6 Astra (September 3), yesterday's lead, with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Muse Spark 1.3 on September 2. MCP: no server and no spec release; newest still the 2026-07-28 stateless specification and the August 22 roadmap update — a seventh consecutive week with no protocol movement. ARXIV: agent-architecture, skills and context-engineering searches returned only out-of-window papers (2601.21557, 2602.12430, 2603.09619, 2606.20631, 2606.20683, 2602.14690), so logged null rather than padded with a stale citation. AGENT FUNDING: no material round dated in window. Crusoe's $3B at a $30B valuation IS dated September 4 but is data-centre capacity, not an agent platform. The week's on-topic consolidation is recorded at its TRUE date and not as news: Palo Alto Networks acquired Console — two years old, AI agents automating routine IT help-desk work (password resets, app access, routine troubleshooting), customers including Ramp, Flock Safety and Scale AI — for about $500M in cash and stock against a $157M pre-deal PitchBook valuation on $29M raised, announced September 1 and reported September 2, to be folded into Cortex. SIGNAGE: an eighteenth consecutive check returned only digital-signage and wayfinding vendor marketing plus general MCP-gateway content; no MCP layer, no API, no protocol for the physical sign trade's permitting and specification work.
bullets.how: NO on the market items. The signage negative is unchanged and now eighteen checks deep, and this report continues to record the open window rather than recommend building into it. The METHOD half is applicable YES and is the day's transferable finding: yesterday's rule was 'a null is as wide as the channels you checked', and today's correction is narrower and more uncomfortable — the channel WAS checked, three separate times, by the corrected rule, and the null was still false, because a release-notes page can gain an entry dated EARLIER than the day you read it. So a null needs a timestamp of its own, and it decays: a channel that was silent yesterday must be RE-READ rather than assumed still silent, and 'silent for N days' must never harden into a claim, because each of those N days is only as good as the moment it was taken. That runs inward exactly as the last one did — brand-insights/latest.json, the flywheel registries and this file's own generated stamp all record when they were written, not when the world last moved.

praxis_lesson: Two findings that turn out to be the same finding. First, /skill-doctor exists now, and it measures the one quantity this ecosystem has never measured — which of ~130 skills actually fire, and what the rest cost in context just by being loaded. A library that only grows is a library nobody has audited, and the fleet has been paying for the unaudited ones on every single turn; the vendor has now made the audit a slash command, so the excuse is gone. Second, and paired with it, ant apply makes skills, agents, environments, memory stores and deployments declarable in files with a plan step and a claude-lock.json lockfile — so the answer to 'which skills do we keep' can be committed rather than remembered. Measure, then declare. Third, the method correction, which is a strictly harder version of yesterday's. Yesterday's lesson was that a null is only as wide as the channels you checked. Today the Platform channel WAS checked — three separate times, by the corrected rule — and the null was still false, because the page gained a September 3 entry that was not there when it was read. A null is therefore not a fact about the world but a MEASUREMENT WITH A TIMESTAMP, and it decays. The operational form is cheap: re-read a silent channel rather than carrying its silence forward, and never let 'silent for N days' harden into a claim, because each of those N days is only as good as the moment it was taken. Same test inward, same as yesterday: every Construct feed that says 'nothing changed' is reporting when it last looked, not what is true now. Fourth, unchanged and now standing a SEVENTH day: claude --version has still not been read on the fleet, and 2.1.260's parentheses bug keeps that a security question rather than housekeeping — and it is now also the only thing standing between this fleet and the skill audit in bullet 1.
